title: DBR-based spectral emissivity selector tuned to 3-5 μm reflection band
scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave stack centered at 4 μm using HfO2/SiO2 pairs will produce high reflectance (low emissivity) in the 3-5 μm band while maintaining sufficient transmittance to allow silicon substrate emission in the 8-13 μm band.
design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflectors create stopbands where reflectance is high when layer optical thicknesses satisfy the quarter-wave condition at a center wavelength. Emissivity equals absorptance per Kirchhoff's law, so high reflectance corresponds to low emissivity. By tuning the Bragg center to 3-5 μm, the stack should suppress emission there while remaining relatively transparent at longer wavelengths where the optical thickness no longer satisfies the Bragg condition.
proposed_topology: air | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | si
soft_objectives: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band
minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band
maintain smooth spectral response without sharp resonant spikes
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count is 20, within the 24 layer limit
all layers are dielectric materials compatible with standard deposition
individual layer thicknesses should remain in practical deposition range (tens to thousands of nm)
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance when each layer optical thickness equals λ/4 at the design wavelength
Recalled: HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the infrared, providing index contrast for Bragg reflection
Recalled: Emissivity equals absorptance for opaque or semi-opaque systems per Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation
Recalled: Bragg stopband width increases with refractive index contrast between alternating layers
Recalled: Silicon substrate is absorptive in the thermal IR and will contribute to emission if the overlying stack is transparent
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology reduces optimization complexity
Quarter-wave starting point provides physically reasonable initial thicknesses
20 layers provides sufficient optical depth for strong reflection in the target band
Dielectric-only stack avoids metallic absorption losses
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 at 3-13 μm wavelengths - the catalog data will determine actual optical behavior
Uncertain: Whether 10 pairs provides sufficient reflectance at 3-5 μm without excessive reflection at 8-13 μm - may need to adjust pair count
Uncertain: Silicon substrate extinction coefficient at these wavelengths affects baseline emission - catalog data required
Uncertain: Whether quarter-wave condition at 4 μm is the optimal center wavelength - 3.5 μm or 4.5 μm might perform better
Risk: If hfo2 or sio2 have significant absorption in 8-13 μm, the stack itself will emit rather than transmit substrate emission
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: air | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat) | si. All 20 dielectric layer thicknesses are independent optimization variables. Target wavelength bands: 3000-5000 nm (minimize emissivity) and 8000-13000 nm (maximize emissivity). Polarization: unpolarized or average of TE and TM. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), si from catalog. Evaluate emissivity as 1 minus reflectance minus transmittance, or directly as absorptance per Kirchhoff's law. Optimize thicknesses to maximize emissivity in 8000-13000 nm while minimizing emissivity in 3000-5000 nm.
